text:
Someone pushed commits to `main` on the remote after you last fetched, so your local `main` isn't a descendant of `origin/main`. Git refuses the push rather than discard their work.

Fix:

```
git pull --rebase origin main
git push
```

That replays your local commits on top of the remote ones. If the rebase hits conflicts, resolve them, `git add` the files, `git rebase --continue`; `git rebase --abort` backs out.

Two notes: if you'd rather not rewrite your local commits, use `git pull` (merge) instead — you get a merge commit. And don't reach for `git push --force` here; it would delete the other person's commits from the remote.
